license_note: The repository LICENSE file is the LFM Open License v1.0, which reuses the Apache License 2.0 text and adds Section 5: the copyright and patent grants are conditioned on a commercial use limitation, and a legal entity with annual revenue of $10,000,000 or more has no licensed right to use the work or a derivative for commercial purposes until it buys a commercial licence from Liquid AI, Inc. Section 5(c) exempts qualified non-profit organizations from the threshold for non-commercial or research purposes, and there is no copyleft, so proprietary fine-tunes are permitted. A revenue ceiling on an otherwise Apache-2.0 grant is a use restriction, so the release is source-available rather than open source. The same terms govern the official GGUF, MLX, and ONNX exports; no separate code licence covers this repository, which ships weights, a chat template, and tokenizer files only.

license_evidence.scope: LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B weights, chat template, and tokenizer files, and every official format export and derivative of them; Section 5 caps free commercial use at legal entities below $10,000,000 annual revenue

access_boundary: This record represents the LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B weight release announced 4 August 2026, the 2.6B dense text-to-text checkpoint of the LFM2.5 line. The LFM2.5-2.6B-Base pre-trained checkpoint, the deprecated LFM2-2.6B and LFM2-2.6B-Exp predecessors, the sibling LFM2.5 sizes and the LFM2.5-VL, LFM2.5-Audio, and Liquid Nanos families, the official GGUF, MLX, and ONNX format exports, the LFM2.5-2.6B-DSpark speculative-decoding drafter, the Liquid Playground and the partner API programme, and OpenRouter's hosted route for the same weights are separate boundaries.
strengths: Developer-published BF16 safetensors checkpoint with official GGUF, MLX, and ONNX exports and a 328M DSpark speculative-decoding drafter, all on the LiquidAI Hugging Face organization

The LFM Open License is published in full on the developer's own site with a plain-language summary, a hosting-platform FAQ, and an explicit Apache 2.0 comparison, and the FAQ confirms the $10 million threshold and the non-profit exemption

First-party model card and documentation cover the hybrid convolution and attention layer layout, parameter count, 34T-token training budget, 128K mid-training context extension, the four post-training stages, the ChatML-like chat template, tool-call syntax, and per-runtime deployment recipes from llama.cpp and MLX through vLLM and SGLang
tradeoffs: The LFM Open License ends the right to use the release for commercial purposes once a legal entity's annual revenue reaches $10 million, so a commercial licence from Liquid AI replaces the free grant at that point
Liquid AI states it does not offer a hosted API of its own; the only documented managed route is OpenRouter, and the Liquid Playground is a rate-limited trial

The deprecations page names successors for retired LFM2 checkpoints and the LFM2.5 line, but the model card publishes no versioning or deprecation commitment for the 2.6B line itself, and the LFM2.5-Encoders and Liquid Nanos families are listed in the same documentation matrix
